newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgacom to get 5.8 bln bfr from state.
newsitem.headline: Belgacom to get 5.8 bln bfr from state.

text.p: Partly state-owned Belgian telecoms firm Belgacom will get 5.8 billion francs from the Belgian government in the form of a capital injection, the government said on Friday.
The money will go to Belgacom's pension funds.
"This 5.8 billion is not government aid. It is an investment by the state in the company," Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene said after the weekly cabinet meeting.
He said the state would take part in a capital increase at Belgacom for which it would receive non-voting, interest-bearing shares.
"After five years we will either get this money back with interest or the shares will be converted into regular shares with voting rights," Deputy Prime Minister Elio di Rupo said.
A team of experts was currently finalising details of the operation, after which it will be put to European Union competition authorities for approval.

On Thursday Di Rupo, who is also Telecommunications Minister, said the injection should be seen in the framework of the Belgacom restructuring, the so-called PTS-programme which focuses mainly on large-scale early retirement and re-training.
He said the injection -- a re-investment in his words -- reflected the government's faith in Belgacom.

The December 1995 sale of half of Belgacom minus one share to a consortium of Ameritech, Singapore Telecom, TeleDanmark and three Belgian investors, earned 73.3 billion francs. More than half went to the financing of a high-speed rail project and the reduction of state debt.
